paragraphs: McGraw Hill is a leading global provider of education solutions for K-12, higher education and professional learning markets. We are helping shape the education industry by providing access to effective learning experiences that improve outcomes and opportunities for all.

McGraw Hill operates at the intersection of proprietary content, software and data, using artificial intelligence to deliver personalized learning experiences at global scale, driving positive outcomes throughout the entire learning lifecycle.
For more than 137 years, McGraw Hill has built one of the world's most recognized education brands with over 100 million active student and educator curriculum licenses worldwide.

Demand for personalized content, delivered via intuitive digital solutions, is reshaping the industry as educators continue to leverage technology, including generative artificial intelligence ("AI"), to meet students where they are in their learning journey.

Over the last decade, we have invested more than $2.0 billion in developing a suite of market-leading digital learning solutions. Our scalable digital solutions rely on shared technology infrastructure, years of collaborative partnerships with leading institutions, expertise in learning science led by a team of approximately 300 software engineers. We utilize our data analytics capabilities to generate continuous feedback loops that drive product and go-to-market innovation, which allows us to simplify workflows while creating meaningful learning experiences that are tailored to the needs of each learner.

At McGraw Hill, we recognize that educational content integrity is of the utmost importance, especially as generative AI becomes more integrated into the learning process. With the proliferation of AI-generated content, the risks of dissemination of inaccurate and low-quality information to learners and educators are heightened, which is why our proprietary content is rigorously researched and designed to meet the highest quality standards. Educational institutions require vetted curriculum aligned to thousands of state, institutional and professional accreditation standards, supported by trusted brands with demonstrated efficacy. As a result, we believe our combination of proprietary content, institutional relationships, learning science expertise and large-scale learning data creates structural barriers to substitution by generic AI systems. Rather than replacing trusted education providers, we believe generative AI will increasingly rely on high‑quality proprietary content and domain‑specific data sources developed by providers like McGraw Hill.

The Company was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware. In July 2025, we completed an initial public offering, in which we issued and sold 24,390,000 shares of our Common Stock (the "initial public offering"). Our Common Stock is currently listed on the NYSE under the symbol "MH." Our fiscal year is a 52-week period ending on March 31.

For the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024, we generated revenue of $2,102.8 million, $2,101.3 million and $1,960.5 million, respectively, and a net income (loss) of $35.3 million, $(85.8) million and $(193.0) million, respectively.
For the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024, we generated Adjusted EBITDA of $744.3 million, $726.8 million and $656.6 million, respectively.
For additional information on Adjusted EBITDA, see "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Non-GAAP Financial Measures."
We leverage our market leading position, proprietary data assets, and global distribution network to drive long term value through the following key growth strategies:

We seek new customers onto our learning solutions with our trusted brand, global go-to-market reach and proprietary digital learning solutions. Our Evergreen delivery model has advanced the state of the industry by delivering on-demand and regularly updated digital content directly to existing learning solutions. By keeping course and support materials fresh and engaging, we eliminate the friction for educators caused by the course refresh cycle and save them time. During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, we derived approximately 68% of Higher Education revenue through our Evergreen delivery model.

Our extensive institutional footprint and product innovation support our land-and-expand strategy through up-selling and cross-selling. We believe our K-12 customers will benefit from our integrated core, supplemental and intervention solutions through improved teacher workflow efficiencies and unique, data-driven insights that support the delivery of personalized learning which also improves retention.

We leverage data-driven insights from billions of longitudinal learning interactions. For the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, McGraw Hill had approximately 26.7 million and 26.2 million paid digital users, respectively, and we recorded more than 25.6 billion learning interactions across McGraw Hill solutions in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, generating insights into student performance and academic growth over time. Learning interactions measures the volume of user-driven educational activities across McGraw Hill platforms, including answering questions, completing assignments, and engaging with learning content. This data captures activity across K-12 platforms (Open Learning, ConnectED, ALEKS), Higher Education (Smartbook, Connect), and Enterprise IDM. For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, coverage expanded to include A3K Literacy, Actively Learn, and additional Connect data.

headings: Risks Related to Our Customer Markets
We face competition from both large, established industry participants and new market entrants, the risks of which are enhanced due to rapid changes in our industry and market.
Increased availability of and support for free or relatively inexpensive products may reduce demand for or negatively impact the pricing of our products.
Generative AI systems may make it easier for competitive instructional materials to be created which could negatively affect demand for or the pricing of our products.
If we fail to adapt and respond effectively to changing technology, evolving industry standards and changing customers' needs or requirements, our platforms may become less competitive.
Increased customer expectations for lower prices or free/discounted bundled products could reduce sales revenue.
Our failure to win new adoptions in certain U.S. states could adversely affect our revenue and operating results.
Changes in state academic standards could affect our market and require investment in new or different products.

Changes in the timing and scope of anticipated levels of federal, state and local education funding available for the purchase of instructional materials could adversely affect purchases for our K-12 products.
Factors that reduce enrollment at colleges and universities could adversely affect demand for our Higher Education products.
The high degree of seasonality of our sales typically results in ebbs and flows in our revenues, which impacts our quarterly operating results and cash flows.
A change from up-front payment by school districts for multi-year licenses could adversely affect our cash flow.
Failure to comply with privacy, accessibility and other laws could have a material adverse impact on our reputation and financial performance.
Defects in our digital products could cause financial loss and reputational damage.
Our business is dependent upon our brand recognition and reputation, and if we fail to maintain or support our brand recognition or reputation, our business could be harmed.
Legal actions against us, including putative class action lawsuits, could be costly to defend and could result in significant damages.
Rapidly changing expectations and standards on environmental, social and governance ("ESG") matters may impact our business, subject us to unforeseen liability or cause harm to our reputation.
Changes in accounting rules could adversely affect our future operating results.
Risks Related to Distribution, Sourcing and Talent
We utilize the services of third-party suppliers, distributors, representatives and retailers for a substantial portion of our sales.
An insufficient supply of, or increases in the costs of, paper could adversely affect our financial results.
Consolidation and concentration in our distribution and retail channels for our Higher Education products could adversely affect our profitability and financial results.
An adverse change in orders or payments by a material reseller could adversely affect our financial results.
Unexpectedly large returns could adversely affect our financial results.
We outsource the performance of many critical operational functions to third parties.
We may not be able to retain or attract the key authors and talented personnel that we need to remain competitive and grow.
A significant increase in operating costs and expenses due to inflation or other causes could have a material adverse effect on our profitability and cash flow.
Risks Related to Our Intellectual Property

Below is a summary of the material risks that make an investment in our Common Stock speculative or risky. This summary does not address all of the risks that we face. Additional discussion of the risks summarized in this risk factor summary, and other risks that we face, can be found in this Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this Form 10-K and our other filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"), before making an investment decision regarding our Common Stock. These risks include, but are not limited to, the following:

•we operate in a highly competitive market, and we may not be able to compete successfully against current and future competitors and/or against low cost or no-cost competitive products, including those that may be produced by other parties through the use of large language models and other artificial intelligence systems;
•our ability to win new markets, adapt to changing state academic standards and anticipate and meet changes in timing and scope of federal, state and local education funding and enrollment;

•the effect of various political and economic issues, including the military conflict in the Middle East, and our ability to comply with laws and regulations we are subject to, both in the United States and internationally;
•our ability to adjust to developments in the economic or regulatory environment;

McGraw Hill is a leading global provider of education solutions for K-12, higher education and professional learning markets. We are helping shape the education industry by providing access to effective learning experiences that improve outcomes and opportunities for all. McGraw Hill operates at the intersection of proprietary content, software and data, using artificial intelligence to deliver personalized learning experiences at global scale, driving positive outcomes throughout the entire learning lifecycle. For more than 137 years, McGraw Hill has built one of the world's most recognized education brands with over 100 million active student and educator curriculum licenses worldwide.

Demand for personalized content, delivered via intuitive digital solutions is reshaping the industry as educators continue to leverage technology, including generative AI, to meet students where they are in their learning journey.
The business is comprised of the following four reportable segments:

•K-12: The Company provides end-to-end core, supplemental and intervention curricula to support the needs of U.S. K-12 schools. The Company sells blended digital and print learning solutions directly to school districts across the United States.

•Higher Education: The Company provides students, instructors and institutions with adaptive digital learning solutions and content, and instructional materials. The primary users of the Company's solutions are students enrolled in two-and four-year non-profit colleges and universities, and to a lesser extent, for-profit institutions. The Company sells its Higher Education solutions to well-known online retailers and distribution partners, who subsequently sell to students. The Company also sells direct to student via its proprietary e-commerce platform.

•Global Professional: The Company provides students, institutions and professionals with comprehensive medical and engineering learning solutions. The Company sells digital learning solutions and print materials which are easily accessible through a broad range of mediums.

•International: The Company is a provider of comprehensive digital and print solutions in more than 100 countries and 80 languages outside of the United States. Through our expansive global distribution network, we serve the needs of learners and educators throughout the world with our K-12 and Higher Education solutions that primarily originate or are adapted from our U.S.-based solutions.

In connection with the Company's initial public offering, on July 23, 2025, the Company converted all of its outstanding Class A voting Common Stock and Class B non-voting Common Stock into a single class of Common Stock on a 1-for-1 basis (the "Stock Conversion") and effected a 1.06555-for-1 stock split (the "Stock Split") of the Company's Common Stock, including the shares of Common Stock underlying outstanding stock options. The par value of the Company's Common Stock was not adjusted and 166,611,519 shares of Common Stock with a par value of $0.01 per share, were outstanding as a result of the Stock Split. All share and per share data has been presented on the basis of the Stock Split for all the periods presented within these consolidated financial statements.

On July 25, 2025, the Company completed its initial public offering in which we issued and sold 24,390,000 shares of our Common Stock at a public offering price of $17.00 per share. The Company received $385.7 million in net proceeds, after deducting $21.8 million of underwriting discounts and commissions and approximately $7.2 million in estimated offering expenses. The underwriters were granted a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 3,658,500 shares of Common Stock from the Selling Stockholder (as defined herein) solely to cover over-allotments. The underwriters did not exercise this option.

Our results of operations have been, and will continue to be, affected by many factors. While these factors present opportunities for our business, they also pose challenges and risks that we must address in order to sustain growth and improve our results of operations.

Our institutional relationships and product innovations support our ability to expand existing customer relationships through up-selling and cross-selling of existing solutions and offering new solutions that address emerging customer needs, which contributes to incremental revenue growth and improved retention. Our ability to increase sales to existing customers will depend on a number of factors, including the level of satisfaction with our solutions, competition, pricing, economic conditions and spending by customers on our solutions.

We seek new customers onto our learning solutions with our brand, global go-to-market reach and product portfolio. Our ability to attract new customers is dependent upon a number of factors, including the features and pricing of our solutions, the effectiveness of our marketing efforts, the marketing and distribution of our solutions and the continued growth in demand for digital learning solutions across the education end-markets we serve. Our Evergreen delivery model provides on-demand and regularly updated digital content directly to existing learning solutions and for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, we derived approximately 68% of Higher Education revenue through this model.

We leverage data-driven insights from billions of learning interactions. For the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, McGraw Hill had approximately 26.7 million and 26.2 million paid digital users, respectively, and we recorded more than 25.6 billion learning interactions, across McGraw Hill solutions in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. These interactions generate insights into student performance and academic growth over time. Our platforms create a continuous data flywheel in which learning interactions generate new insights that improve our AI models and enhance personalization, driving increased adoption, engagement and improved customer retention.

paragraphs: McGraw Hill 是 K-12、高等教育及專業學習市場中，提供教育解決方案的領導者。我們透過提供有效的學習體驗，改善學習成果與機會，來塑造教育產業。
McGraw Hill 位於專有內容、軟體與數據的交會點，運用人工智慧，於全球規模提供個人化學習體驗，驅動整個學習生命週期中的正面成果。
超過 137 年來，McGraw Hill 已建立全球最知名的教育品牌之一，擁有超過 1 億個 active 學生與教育者課程授權。
對個人化內容的需求，透過直覺的數位解決方案進行交付，正在重塑產業。教育者持續運用科技，包括生成式人工智慧（"AI"），以在學習旅程中與學生接觸。
近十年來，本公司已投資超過 2.0 十億美元用以開發一套市場領先的數位學習解決方案。我們的可擴展數位解決方案依賴共用的科技基礎設施、多年與知名機構的合作夥伴關係，以及由約 300 名軟體工程師組成的團隊所領導的學習科學專業知識。我們運用資料分析能力，產生持續的反饋迴路，推動產品與市場進入策略的創新，這使我們得以簡化作業流程，同時創造符合每位學習者需求的有意義學習體驗。

在 McGraw Hill，我們認知到教育內容的完整性至關重要，尤其當生成式 AI 越來越多地整合進學習過程中。隨著 AI 生成內容的普及，將不準確與低品質資訊散佈給學習者與教育者的風險也隨之提高，這就是為何我們的專有內容經過嚴謹研究與設計，以符合最高品質標準。教育機構需要經過驗證的課程，符合數千個州、機構與專業認證標準，並由有顯著成效的受信任品牌支持。因此，我們相信我們的專有內容、機構關係、學習科學專業知識與大規模學習數據的組合，創造出結構性的替代障礙，使一般 AI 系統無法取代。我們認為生成式 AI 將越來越依賴由像 McGraw Hill 這樣的提供者所開發的高品質專有內容與特定領域數據來源。
本公司於德拉瓦州法律下設立。2025 年 7 月，我們完成首次公開發行（initial public offering），發行並銷售 24,390,000 份本公司普通股（the "initial public offering"）。本公司普通股目前於紐約證券交易所（NYSE）上市，代號為 "MH"。本公司會計年度為 52 週，於 3 月 31 日結止。
截至 2026 年 3 月 31 日、2025 年 3 月 31 日及 2024 年 3 月 31 日會計年度，本公司營業收入分別為 2,102.8 百萬美元、2,101.3 百萬美元及 1,960.5 百萬美元，淨收入（虧損）分別為 35.3 百萬美元、(85.8) 百萬美元及 (193.0) 百萬美元。
有關調整後營業利益（Adjusted EBITDA）之更多資訊，請參閱「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析—非GAAP財務指標」。
本公司利用市場領導地位、專屬資料資產及全球通路網路，透過以下關鍵成長策略來驅動長期價值：
本公司透過受信賴的品牌、全球行銷通路及專屬數位學習解決方案，尋求新客戶加入我們的學習解決方案。我們的Evergreen交付模式已提升產業的水準，透過直接向現有學習解決方案提供即時且定期更新的數位內容。透過保持課程與支援資料的新鮮與吸引力，我們消除了教師因課程更新週期所造成的摩擦，並為教師節省時間。在會計年度截至2026年3月31日，我們透過Evergreen交付模式取得約68%的高階教育收入。
我們廣泛的機構網路與產品創新支持我們的「擴展策略」（land-and-expand strategy），透過 upsell 與 cross-sell 來增加銷售。我們相信K-12客戶將從我們整合的核心、補充與幹預解決方案中受益，透過改善教師工作流程效率與獨特的數據驅動見解，支持個性化學習的交付，同時也提高學生留存率。

我們運用來自數十億筆縱向學習互動的數據驅動洞察。於截至2026年3月31日及2025年3月31日的會計年度，麥格勞希爾約有26.7百萬及26.2百萬已付款數位使用者，於截至2026年3月31日的會計年度，我們在麥格勞希爾解決方案中記錄了超過25.6十億筆學習互動，產生對學生表現及學術成長的洞察。學習互動衡量使用者在麥格勞希爾平台上的教育活動體積，包括回答問題、完成作業及與學習內容互動。此數據涵蓋K-12平台（Open Learning、ConnectED、ALEKS）、高等教育（Smartbook、Connect）及企業IDM。於截至2026年3月31日的會計年度，覆蓋範圍擴展至包含A3K Literacy、Actively Learn及額外的Connect數據。

McGraw Hill為全球K-12、高等教育及專業學習市場提供領導性的教育解決方案。我們透過提供有效的學習體驗，改善學習成果與機會，來塑造教育產業。McGraw Hill在專屬內容、軟體與數據的交會點運作，利用人工智慧提供全球規模的個人化學習體驗，推動整個學習生命週期的正面成果。超過137年來，McGraw Hill已建立全球最知名的教育品牌之一，擁有超過100百萬的活躍學生與教育者課程授權。
透過直覺數位解決方案提供的個性化內容，正在重塑產業。教育者持續利用科技，包括生成式AI，以符合學生在學習旅程中的需求。
業務包含以下四個應報告分部：
•K-12：本公司提供完整的K-12美國學校所需的核心、補充與幹預課程。本公司直接向美國各學校學區銷售結合數位與印刷的學習解決方案。
•高等教育：本公司為學生、教師與機構提供適應性數位學習解決方案與內容，以及教學材料。本公司解決方案的主要使用者為註冊於非營利兩年制與四年制大學與學院的學生，其次為營利機構。本公司透過知名線上零售商與分銷夥伴銷售其高等教育解決方案，這些零售商隨後銷售給學生。本公司也透過其專屬電商平台直接銷售給學生。
•全球專業：本公司為學生、機構與專業人士提供完整的醫療與工程學習解決方案。本公司銷售數位學習解決方案與印刷材料，這些材料可透過廣泛的媒介輕易取得。
•國際：本公司為超過100個國家與80種語言（美國除外）的學習者與教育者提供完整的數位與印刷解決方案。透過我們廣大的全球分銷網路，我們以來自美國的解決方案或經調整後的版本，服務全球的學習者與教育者。

本公司於2025年7月23日，因首次公開發行股票，將所有未償還的A類投票普通股與B類非投票普通股，按1股換1股的比例轉換為單一類別的普通股（"股票轉換"），並實施普通股的1.06555股換1股的股票分割（"股票分割"），包括所有未償還股票選擇權所對應的普通股。本公司普通股的票面價值未調整，經股票分割後，本公司共有166,611,519股普通股，每股票面價值為0.01美元。所有股數及每股數據均根據股票分割後的基礎呈現，適用於這些合併財務報表中所列示的所有期間。
本公司於2025年7月25日完成首次公開發行股票，發行並銷售24,390,000股普通股，每股公開發行價格為17.00美元。本公司在扣除21.8百萬美元的經紀佣金與折扣及約7.2百萬美元的預估發行費用後，共收到385.7百萬美元的淨資金。經紀人獲得了30日的選擇權，可購買最多3,658,500股普通股，以覆蓋過量發行部分，但經紀人未行使此選擇權。
本公司營運成果已受到許多因素的影響，且未來仍將持續受到這些因素的影響。雖然這些因素為本公司業務帶來機會，但也同時帶來挑戰與風險，我們必須解決這些問題以維持成長並改善營運成果。
本公司與機構客戶的關係及產品創新，支持我們透過現有解決方案的 upsell 與 cross-sell，以及提供符合新興客戶需求的解決方案，來擴大現有客戶關係，這有助於增加收入成長與改善客戶留存率。本公司增加現有客戶銷售的能力，取決於多種因素，包括客戶對我們解決方案的滿意度、競爭情況、價格、總體經濟狀況及客戶在我們解決方案上的支出。

我們透過品牌、全球市場推廣能力與產品組合，尋求將新客戶引入我們的學習解決方案。我們吸引新客戶的能力取決於多種因素，包括解決方案的特色與價格、我們行銷活動的成效、解決方案的行銷與分銷，以及我們所服務的教育終端市場對數位學習解決方案需求的持續成長。我們的 Evergreen 配送模式可為現有學習解決方案提供即時且定期更新的數位內容，於2026年3月31日財務年度結訖，我們約有68%的高等教育收入來自此模式。

我們運用來自數十億學習互動的數據驅動洞察。於截至2026年3月31日及2025年3月31日的會計年度，麥格勞希爾分別擁有約26.7百萬及26.2百萬付費數位用戶，且我們在截至2026年3月31日的會計年度中，於麥格勞希爾解決方案上記錄了超過25.6十億學習互動。這些互動提供了學生表現及學術成長的洞察。我們的平台創造出一個持續的數據飛輪，學習互動產生新的洞察，改進我們的AI模型並提升個人化程度，推動更高的採用率、參與度及改善客戶留存率。

headings: 與我們客戶市場相關的風險
我們面臨來自大型成熟產業參與者及新市場進場者的競爭，由於產業與市場快速變動，此等風險更顯突出。
免費或相對廉價產品的可取得性與支援增加，可能降低對我們產品的需求或對我們產品的定價產生負面影響。
生成式 AI 系統可能使競爭性教學材料的製作變得更容易，這可能會對我們產品的需求或定價產生負面影響。
若我們未能有效適應並回應技術變動、產業標準演進及客戶需求或要求的改變，我們的平台可能變得較不具競爭力。
客戶對更低價格或免費/折扣組合產品的期待增加，可能降低銷售收入。
我們未能在美國某些州取得新採用，可能會對我們的收入與營運結果產生不利影響。
學術標準的變更可能影響我們的市場，並需要投資於新的或不同的產品。
聯邦、州及地方教育經費預期水準的時間與範圍變更，可能不利於我們 K-12 產品的採購。
大學院校入學人數減少的因素可能不利於我們高教產品的需求。
我們銷售的高季節性特徵通常導致營收出現波動，這會影響我們的季度營運結果與現金流。
由學校區由 upfront 支付多年度授權費變更為其他支付方式，可能不利於我們的現金流。
未能遵守隱私權、可近性及其他法律，可能對我們的聲譽與財務表現造成重大不利影響。
我們數位產品的瑕疵可能導致財務損失與聲譽損害。
本公司業務依賴於品牌認知度與聲譽，若未能維持或支撐品牌認知度與聲譽，將可能對本公司業務造成損害。
針對本公司的法律訴訟，包括可能的集體訴訟，將可能導致高昂的 defence 成本，並可能造成重大賠償。
對於環境、社會及治理（"ESG"）事項的快速變動的期待與標準，可能影響本公司業務，使本公司面臨未預見的責任，或對本公司聲譽造成損害。
會計準則的變動可能對本公司未來的營運結果造成不利影響。
與分銷、來源及人才相關的風險
本公司對於銷售額的 substantially portion 係透過第三方供應商、分銷商、代表及零售商之服務進行。
紙張供應不足，或紙張成本增加，可能對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司 Higher Education 產品在分銷與零售通路的集中化與整併，可能對本公司獲利能力與財務結果造成不利影響。
不利的訂單或付款變動可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
意外的大量退貨可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
我們將許多關鍵作業功能委託第三方執行。
我們可能無法留住或吸引所需的關鍵作者及優秀人才以維持競爭力並實現成長。
由於通貨膨脹或其他原因導致營運成本及費用顯著增加，可能對我們的獲利能力及現金流產生重大負面影響。
與我們智慧財產權相關的風險
paragraphs: 許多因素可能會嚴重不利於我們的業務、營運結果、財務狀況及/或本公司普通股與發行在外的債務證券的價值。這些因素包括但不限於下列風險與不確定性。這些披露內容反映本公司對可能嚴重不利於本公司及其證券的相關因素的信念與觀點。提及過去事件僅作為範例，並非完整列出或表示這些因素是否已發生過，或其未來發生的可能性。
以下為使投資本公司普通股成為投機性或風險性投資的關鍵風險摘要。此摘要並未涵蓋我們所面臨的所有風險。有關本風險因素摘要中所提及風險及其他我們所面臨的風險之進一步討論，可參閱本年度報告表10-K第1A項，並應與本表10-K及其他向美國證券交易委員會（"SEC"）所提交的文件一併審慎考量，以作為投資本公司普通股的決策依據。這些風險包括但不限於下列：
•我們營運於一個高度競爭的市場，我們可能無法成功與現有及未來的競爭對手競爭，並/或與低成本或無成本的競爭產品競爭，包括可能由其他方透過大型語言模型及其他人工智慧系統所生產的產品；
•我們能否拓展新市場、適應變動的州級教育標準，並預測及符合聯邦、州及地方教育經費與入學人數的時間與範疇變動；
•各種政治與經濟議題的影響，包括中東地區的軍事衝突，以及我們能否遵守我們所受的美國與國際法律與法規；
•我們能否適應經濟或法規環境的變動發展；
